source: California Code of Civil Procedure, Parts 2 (Civil Actions)

rules.summary: Personal delivery of the summons and complaint is the primary method; substituted service on a competent member of the household or a person in charge at the usual place of business is permitted when personal service can't reasonably be accomplished, followed by mailing a copy.

rules.topic: Time to respond to a complaint
rules.summary: A defendant generally has 30 days after service of the summons to file an answer or other responsive pleading.

A party may move for summary judgment (or summary adjudication of specific issues) on the ground there is no triable issue of material fact; motions generally must be filed and heard within statutory notice windows before trial.

source: Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, Part II (Rules of Practice in District and County Courts)

rules.summary: Citation is typically served by a sheriff, constable, or authorized process server, delivering a copy to the defendant in person or leaving it with someone over 16 at the defendant's usual place of abode; substituted service requires court authorization.
Texas's distinctive rule: the answer is due on the Monday next after the expiration of 20 days from the date of service — not a flat 20- or 30-day count like most states.

A party may move for summary judgment on the ground there is no genuine issue of material fact; the motion and supporting evidence must be filed and served on the adverse party a minimum number of days before the hearing.

rulesBody: New York Civil Practice Law and Rules (CPLR)
source: New York Civil Practice Law and Rules, Article 3 (Jurisdiction and Service, Appearance and Choice of Court) and Article 32 (Accelerated Judgment)

rules.summary: Personal delivery to the person is the primary method; CPLR § 308 also permits delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion at the defendant's residence or business plus a follow-up mailing, and other alternatives when those aren't practicable.
Generally 20 days to answer after personal delivery of the summons within New York State, or 30 days if service was made by another method or the defendant was served outside the state.

A party may move for summary judgment after issue is joined, on the ground the cause of action or defense has no merit as a matter of law; the court must deny the motion if a genuine, material factual dispute exists.

source: Florida Rules of Civil Procedure, and Florida Statutes Chapter 48 (Process and Service of Process)

rules.citation: Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.070; Fla. Stat. ch. 48
rules.summary: A summons and complaint are generally served by a sheriff or certified process server, delivering the papers to the defendant personally or per the substituted-service methods set out in Florida Statutes Chapter 48.
A defendant generally must serve an answer or other responsive pleading within 20 days after service of the complaint.
A party may move for summary judgment on the ground there is no genuine dispute as to any material fact; Florida's rule was rewritten in 2021 to track the federal Rule 56 standard more closely.

source: Pennsylvania Rules of Civil Procedure, Chapter 400 (Process) and Chapter 1000 (Actions at Law)

rules.summary: Original process is generally served by handing a copy to the defendant, or to an adult member of the household at the defendant's residence, among other permitted methods.

Every pleading subsequent to the complaint is generally due within 20 days after service of the preceding pleading. Pennsylvania's distinctive notice-to-defend / ten-day-notice practice governs when a default judgment can actually be entered for a failure to respond — a separate mechanism from the 20-day pleading deadline itself.
A party may move for summary judgment after the relevant pleadings are closed, on the ground there is no genuine issue of material fact as to a necessary element of a claim or defense.
